newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures reverse direction, head down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures reverse direction, head down.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE robusta coffee futures reversed an upward trend to end down on Tuesday but the losses were minimised by good buying underneath.
Robusta's fall mirrored those in New York arabicas which traders said was expected after Monday's explosive rise to new contract highs, basis May.
London's July stood $14 lower at $1,655 after an intraday low of $1,685. Traders said the contract could attract keen sellers at $1,700.
All eyes centred on the on-going truck drivers' strike in key grower Colombia. Union officials said on Tuesday the workers action, which entered a third day, could last all week.
"The Colombian problem will remain for the time being," said one. "It may or may not have any impact on the market."
The Colombia strike coincided with Tuesday's first delivery day for New York's May contract.
No notices were issued on Tuesday. Traders said there could be a potential supply squeeze as the open interest of 4,056 lots remained large against deliverable coffee stocks of just 250 lots.
"The problem is there is not enough coffee," the trader said.
May's premium to second-month July remained wide at 23 cents a lb.
In London, there had been a gradual unwinding of the May position ahead of its first tender day on May 1.
By the close of business on Monday, May's uncovered positions fell by 642 lots to 9,925.
May/July switches were traded at $28 under and July/Sept $8-$10 under.
Chartwise, the top of July's range was marked by a chart gap between Monday's high of $1,705 and the March 12 low of $1,730.
Strong support rested near $1,600, a level amid an area where several moving averages and trendlines meet, analysts said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
